[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance document defines when to use **Next.js** versus **plain React (Webpack 5)** for frontend application development at Gainwell Technologies. Both are React-based and are approved technologies, but they serve fundamentally different architectural roles within the enterprise micro-frontend strategy. Selecting the wrong tool for the context creates unnecessary complexity, breaks module composition patterns, or leaves teams without capabilities they need (SSR, auth, SEO).
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

Following this guidance ensures:

- Teams select the right tool for their application's role in the architecture, reducing rework
- Micro-frontend Module Federation composition remains technically feasible
- Authentication, session management, and HIPAA compliance are handled consistently
- Build times, bundle sizes, and Core Web Vitals targets are achievable without over-engineering
- Hiring and onboarding friction is reduced by standardizing on well-documented technology paths

page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

- **ASP.NET Migration**: State MMIS applications requiring migration to React-based architecture must have the migration target stack selected carefully — choosing Next.js for a Module Federation remote module blocks the composition architecture.
- **Multi-Team Independence**: The micro-frontend strategy enables teams to deploy independently multiple times per day without coordinating with other teams, only achievable if module composition via Webpack Module Federation works correctly. Next.js has limited Module Federation support that must be accounted for in decisions.
- **Regulatory Compliance**: HIPAA PHI requirements, Section 508 accessibility, and FedRAMP mandate specific rendering, authentication, and security header capabilities. Next.js provides these more natively than a bare React SPA.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#strategic-alignment]

#### Strategic Alignment

React is established as the **primary recommended framework** for Gainwell's enterprise applications (post-ASP.NET migration) per the Enterprise Micro-Frontend Architecture Strategy white paper. Both Next.js and plain React are approved paths within this strategy — this guidance resolves which to use and when.

page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Teams making greenfield or migration stack decisions frequently conflate Next.js and plain React because both are "React." Next.js provides a superset of React capabilities that introduce constraints (notably limited Module Federation support) that break the enterprise micro-frontend composition architecture if a remote module is built with Next.js. Conversely, teams building standalone portals or shell applications using plain React + Webpack unnecessarily forgo Next.js capabilities (SSR, built-in routing, NextAuth.js, automatic code splitting, Core Web Vitals tooling) that are directly relevant to HIPAA/security compliance and portal requirements.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#impact-assessment]

#### Impact Assessment

- Choosing Next.js for a federated remote module may require significant rework when Module Federation composition is required
- Choosing plain React for a shell application or standalone portal requires manual configuration for authentication, routing, SSR, and performance tooling that Next.js provides out of the box
- Inconsistent choices across teams fragment the codebase and increase maintenance overhead

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#principle-1-role-before-technology]

#### Principle 1: Role Before Technology

**Description:** Determine the application's architectural role first — shell, remote module, or standalone — before selecting the technology. The role determines the technology, not the other way around.

**Rationale:** Next.js and plain React have fundamentally different capabilities relative to Module Federation. Reversing the decision sequence (picking technology first) is the primary cause of rework.

**Application:** Use the [Decision Framework](#decision-framework) below. Role classification before writing any code avoids rework later.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#principle-2-module-federation-is-the-composition-boundary]

#### Principle 2: Module Federation is the Composition Boundary

**Description:** Module Federation is the mandated runtime composition mechanism for the enterprise micro-frontend architecture. Any technology decision that compromises Module Federation compatibility requires an approved architectural exception.

**Rationale:** Module Federation enables independent deployment of micro-frontends without coordinating builds. This is the mechanism that unlocks team autonomy — teams can deploy their modules multiple times per day without waiting on other teams. Anything that breaks this breaks team autonomy.

**Application:** If a team needs Module Federation (i.e., the application is a federated remote module), use plain React + Webpack 5 with `ModuleFederationPlugin` per [STD-APP-FE-001 §3.1](../../../../standards/application/frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md) and [ADR-APP-004](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-004-mfe-platform-layer-selection.md). Do not use Next.js as a federated remote without a validated Module Federation plugin evaluation and Architecture Review Board approval.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#principle-3-nextjs-for-the-outer-shell-and-portals]

#### Principle 3: Next.js for the Outer Shell and Portals

**Description:** Next.js is the preferred technology for shell applications (the host that composes remote modules) and for standalone portals that do not participate in Module Federation as remotes.

**Rationale:** Shell applications and standalone portals benefit from Next.js's SSR prop injection (delivering user context before first render), NextAuth.js integration with PingOne OIDC, automatic code splitting, and built-in performance tooling — all without custom configuration.

**Application:** If the application is a shell that loads remote modules, or a standalone portal with no Module Federation remote requirements, default to Next.js unless a specific constraint prohibits it.

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#approach-1-nextjs-shell-application]

#### Approach 1: Next.js Shell Application

**Overview:** The shell application is the host that composes independently deployed micro-frontend remote modules at runtime via Module Federation. Built with Next.js, it provides routing, authentication session management, shared context injection, and the outer layout.

**When to Use:**

- The application hosts/composes federated remote modules from other teams
- Server-side rendering of the initial page load improves performance or SEO
- Authentication must be handled centrally with session management (NextAuth.js + PingOne OIDC)
- The team needs built-in Core Web Vitals tooling without custom Webpack configuration

**Implementation:**

- Use Next.js App Router for file-based routing
- Integrate NextAuth.js for PingOne OIDC/MFA per STD-TEC-NXT-003
- Provide shell context to remote modules via `getServerSideProps` + `MfeContextProvider` (see PTN-APP-MFE-009)
- Consume federated remotes via dynamic import with `React.lazy` / `Suspense`
- Configure `Content-Security-Policy` headers scoping `script-src` to specific CDN origins (no `unsafe-inline`; `unsafe-eval` prohibited); SRI hashes required on every `remoteEntry.js` load — a wildcard `script-src *` negates SRI entirely. Refer to [STD-SEC-APP-001 §3.4](../../../../standards/security/application/STD-SEC-APP-001-application-security.md) for the enterprise-standard security header baseline

**Benefits:**

- SSR props injection eliminates client-side bootstrap delay for micro-frontend context
- NextAuth.js handles token refresh, RBAC, and JWT — reduces HIPAA auth complexity
- Automatic per-route code splitting enforced by framework

- Turbopack (future) provides build performance path

**Considerations:**

- The shell itself should NOT be exposed as a Module Federation remote
- Remote module URLs must be managed at runtime (via manifest API or environment variables) to avoid shell rebuilds on every module deployment

---
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#approach-2-plain-react--webpack-5-federated-remote-module]

#### Approach 2: Plain React + Webpack 5 (Federated Remote Module)

**Overview:** Independently deployable micro-frontend modules that expose domain-specific UI — Claims, Provider, Member, Analytics, etc. — via Webpack Module Federation `remoteEntry.js`. Built with plain React + TypeScript + Webpack 5 to maximize Module Federation compatibility and enable tiny, cacheable bundles.

**When to Use:**

- The application is a federated remote that will be dynamically loaded by a shell at runtime

- The module must expose components or routes to other applications via `remoteEntry.js`
- The module must share singleton dependencies (React, react-dom, design system) with the shell
- The team deploys independently to CDN (AWS CloudFront + S3 or Azure CDN + Blob Storage)

**Implementation:**

- Use Webpack 5 with `ModuleFederationPlugin` configured with `name`, `filename: 'remoteEntry.js'`, `exposes`, and `shared` singletons

- Shared dependencies: `react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`, `@gainwell/design-system` — all `singleton: true` with `requiredVersion`
- Bundle target ≤500KB gzipped; enable code splitting within the module
- Expose a `mount` function (not a full React app bootstrap) so the shell can control rendering lifecycle
- Implement PHI cleanup on unmount — clear component state and Zustand store slices

**Benefits:**

- Native Module Federation support — full control over shared dependency versions
- Independent CDN deployment with semantic versioning (`/claims/v1.2.3/remoteEntry.js`)
- Module bundles are cacheable independently — a Claims release does not invalidate Provider cache
- Enables A/B testing by routing traffic to versioned module URLs

**Considerations:**

- **Webpack 5 is the required build tool** for all new remote modules — use `ModuleFederationPlugin` from `webpack/container` per [STD-APP-FE-001 §3.1](../../../../standards/application/frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md) and [ADR-APP-004](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-004-mfe-platform-layer-selection.md). RSpack is the planned evolution path when Platform Engineering publishes the validated scaffold
- Module must not self-bootstrap (no `ReactDOM.render` at module root) — mount/unmount lifecycle is shell-driven

---
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#approach-3-react--webpack-5-standalone-application-no-module-federation]

#### Approach 3: React + Webpack 5 (Standalone Application, No Module Federation)

**Overview:** For new standalone React applications that do not participate in Module Federation — internal tools, admin dashboards, embedded widgets — Webpack 5 is the required build tool, consistent with MFE remote modules. This removes the need to migrate later if Module Federation requirements emerge.

**When to Use:**

- New greenfield application with no Module Federation remote requirements
- Internal tooling or low-complexity admin interface
- Standalone SPA that is not a Next.js portal

**Implementation:**

- Use Webpack 5 with the same base configuration as MFE remote modules (per STD-APP-FE-001 §3.1), omitting the `ModuleFederationPlugin` unless and until federation is required
- State management via Zustand; server state via TanStack Query
- Authentication via PingOne SDK directly (no NextAuth.js) — implement the Authorization Code + PKCE flow; the implicit flow is prohibited. Refer to [STD-SEC-AUTHN-001](../../../../standards/security/authentication/STD-SEC-AUTHN-001-authentication-implementation.md) for required token lifetimes, secure storage, and session management requirements
- If Module Federation requirements emerge later, add `ModuleFederationPlugin` to the existing config — no bundler migration required

**Benefits:**

- No bundler migration if Module Federation is added later
- Consistent toolchain and CI/CD pipeline shape across all React applications
- Shared `@gainwell/mfe-webpack-base` config package applies to standalone and federated apps equally

**Considerations:**

- Webpack build times for standalone apps (no Module Federation overhead) are lower than for federated modules and are acceptable for the toolchain consistency benefit — establish a project-specific baseline during initial setup
- Vite is not approved for any new React application in the enterprise estate (see STD-APP-FE-001 §3.1 STD-FE-002)

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#best-practice-1-provide-phi-context-via-shell-props-not-global-store]

#### Best Practice 1: Provide PHI Context via Shell Props, Not Global Store

**Description:** In a Next.js shell, use `getServerSideProps` + `MfeContextProvider` to inject user context (identifiers, tenant, permissions) into remote modules. Remote modules fetch PHI from authenticated backend APIs using these opaque identifiers — PHI never enters the shell props or any global state store.

**Rationale:** HIPAA Security Rule §164.312(a)(1) prohibits PHI in module bundles, CDN assets, or serialized DevTools state. Server-side prop injection gives modules the context they need without embedding PHI in the JavaScript runtime composition layer.

**Implementation:** See [PTN-APP-MFE-009 Shell-Provided Props Pattern](../../../../patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-009-shell-provided-props-pattern.md) for the full implementation.

**Success Indicators:** PHI never appears in Redux DevTools, React DevTools, browser console logs, or CDN-hosted bundle content.
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#best-practice-2-pin-shared-dependency-versions-across-shell-and-remotes]

#### Best Practice 2: Pin Shared Dependency Versions Across Shell and Remotes

**Description:** In Module Federation shared configuration, always specify `requiredVersion` for React, react-dom, react-router-dom, and the design system. The shell controls the singleton instance; remotes consume it.

**Rationale:** Version mismatches between shell and remote cause duplicate React instances, breaking hooks and context. This is the most common Module Federation production failure mode.

**Implementation:**

```javascript
shared: {
  react: { singleton: true, requiredVersion: '^18.2.0' },
  'react-dom': { singleton: true, requiredVersion: '^18.2.0' },
  'react-router-dom': { singleton: true, requiredVersion: '^6.8.0' },

  '@gainwell/design-system': { singleton: true, requiredVersion: '^2.0.0' },
}
```

**Success Indicators:** Zero "Invalid hook call" errors in production; Module Federation runtime negotiates a single shared instance confirmed in browser DevTools network tab (one `react.js` chunk load, not multiple).
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#best-practice-3-implement-per-module-phi-cleanup-on-unmount]

#### Best Practice 3: Implement Per-Module PHI Cleanup on Unmount

**Description:** Every remote module that handles PHI must implement a cleanup function invoked when the shell unmounts the module — clearing component state, Zustand store slices, and any pending API calls.

**Rationale:** HIPAA Security Rule requires PHI cleared from browser memory on session timeout and module navigation. In a micro-frontend architecture, module unmount is the natural cleanup boundary.

**Implementation:**

```typescript
// In module mount function
return function unmount() {
  claimsStore.setState({ data: null }); // Clear Zustand store
  setClaimData(null);                   // Clear component state
  abortController.abort();             // Cancel in-flight API calls
};
```

**Success Indicators:** Browser memory profiler shows no retained PHI objects after module route change; confirmed via HIPAA compliance audit.

page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#pitfall-1-using-nextjs-as-a-module-federation-remote]

#### Pitfall 1: Using Next.js as a Module Federation Remote

**Description:** Teams build a micro-frontend with Next.js (for its DX benefits) and then attempt to expose it as a Module Federation remote via `next-module-federation` or similar plugins.

**Impact:** Module Federation support in Next.js is non-native and requires third-party plugins with limited maturity. Shared dependency negotiation is unreliable, risking duplicate React instances, broken hooks, and inconsistent design system rendering across the suite.

**Prevention:** Apply the Role Before Technology principle. If the application is a federated remote, use plain React + Webpack 5. If it is a shell or standalone, use Next.js.

**Mitigation:** If already built with Next.js and Module Federation is now required, evaluate the `@module-federation/nextjs-mf` plugin in an isolated environment, validate shared singleton behavior, and obtain Architecture Review Board approval before promoting to production.
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#pitfall-2-global-redux-store-for-phi-in-multi-module-architecture]

#### Pitfall 2: Global Redux Store for PHI in Multi-Module Architecture

**Description:** Teams use Redux (or Zustand with `persist` middleware) to share PHI (member records, claim data) between the shell and remote modules via a shared store exposed through Module Federation.

**Impact:** Redux DevTools exposes full store state in the browser. `persist` middleware writes PHI to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`, violating HIPAA §164.312(a)(1). Cross-module Redux coupling also breaks module independence.

**Prevention:** Use opaque identifiers (claim IDs, member IDs) in cross-module communication. Each module fetches its own PHI from authenticated backend APIs. Use Zustand (no DevTools by default) scoped to the module, not shared across the Module Federation scope.

**Mitigation:** Audit existing Redux usage for PHI in state slices and action payloads. Remove PHI, replacing with identifiers. Disable Redux DevTools in production builds via `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'` guard.
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#pitfall-3-introducing-vite-outside-the-approved-stack]

#### Pitfall 3: Introducing Vite Outside the Approved Stack

**Description:** Teams choose Vite for a new standalone or remote module application due to faster local build times.

**Impact:** Vite is not approved for any new React application in the enterprise estate (STD-APP-FE-001 §3.1 STD-FE-002). Introducing it creates a one-off toolchain that cannot reuse the `@gainwell/mfe-webpack-base` shared config, requires separate CI/CD pipeline maintenance, and requires a bundler migration if Module Federation is added later.

**Prevention:** All new React applications use Webpack 5 regardless of whether they participate in Module Federation. Apply the shared base config; omit `ModuleFederationPlugin` for standalone apps.

**Mitigation:** If Vite is already in use on an existing application, plan a Webpack 5 migration using the `@gainwell/mfe-webpack-base` reference scaffold. Raise via the Architecture Review Board if a timeline exception is needed.

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#decision-point-1-is-this-application-a-module-federation-remote]

#### Decision Point 1: Is This Application a Module Federation Remote?

**Context:** A Module Federation remote is a micro-frontend that exposes a `remoteEntry.js` consumed by a shell or other host application at runtime.

**Options:**

- Yes — the application exposes components/routes to other applications via Module Federation
- No — the application is self-contained or consumes remotes but does not expose them

**Criteria:** Will other applications load this application's components at runtime via `import('url/remoteEntry.js')`?

**Recommendation:** If **Yes** → use **plain React + Webpack 5**. If **No** → proceed to Decision Point 2.

---
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#decision-point-2-does-the-application-need-ssr-built-in-routing-or-centralized-auth]

#### Decision Point 2: Does the Application Need SSR, Built-in Routing, or Centralized Auth?

**Context:** Standalone portals, shell applications, and any application with SEO requirements, complex auth flows (OIDC + MFA + RBAC), or SSR performance requirements benefit from Next.js.

**Options:**

- Yes — the application is a shell, a standalone portal, or a public-facing UI requiring SEO/SSR
- No — the application is a simple internal tool, admin UI, or prototype

**Criteria:** Does the application need any of: server-side rendering, NextAuth.js session management, built-in file-based routing, or automatic image/font optimization?

**Recommendation:** If **Yes** → use **Next.js**. If **No** → use **React + Vite** (simpler builds, no SSR overhead).

---

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#recommended-tools]

#### Recommended Tools

| Tool Category | Tool Name | Purpose | Usage Guidelines |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shell framework | Next.js 14+ App Router | Shell applications, standalone portals | Use for all non-remote-module React applications |
| Remote bundler | Webpack 5 + ModuleFederationPlugin | Federated remote modules | Required for all Module Federation remotes |
| Standalone bundler | Vite 5+ | Non-federated standalone apps | Use only when Module Federation is not required |
| Auth | NextAuth.js + PingOne SDK | OIDC/MFA session management in Next.js | Next.js shell applications only |
| State (global) | Zustand | Module-scoped global state | One store per micro-frontend module; no PHI in state |
| Server state | TanStack Query (React Query) | API data fetching and caching | All applications; replaces manual fetch/useEffect patterns |
| Forms | React Hook Form + Zod | Form state and validation | All applications |
| Testing | Vitest + React Testing Library | Unit and component tests | All applications |
| E2E Testing | Playwright | Cross-browser E2E | Shell integration tests; per-module smoke tests |
| Bundle analysis | Webpack Bundle Analyzer | Validate ≤500KB bundle target | Run on every remote module build |
| Monorepo | Turborepo or Nx | Multi-module build orchestration | When 3+ modules share a repository |

page_texts.52:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#use-case-1-claims-processing-micro-frontend-remote-module]

### Use Case 1: Claims Processing Micro-Frontend (Remote Module)

**Scenario Description:** The Claims team builds a federated remote module serving claim search, detail, adjudication workflow, and submission for embedding in the Enterprise™ shell.

**Context:** Module Federation remote; must share React and design system singletons with shell; independent CDN deployment per PR/release.

**Guidance Application:** Plain React + Webpack 5. `ModuleFederationPlugin` configured with `exposes: { './ClaimsApp': './src/ClaimsApp' }`. Shared singletons with `requiredVersion`. Module-scoped Zustand store cleared on unmount. PHI fetched at runtime via authenticated API using opaque `claimId` identifiers from shell context.

**Success Factors:** Module composition verified in integration environment before production promotion. Bundle ≤500KB gzipped confirmed via Bundle Analyzer.

page_texts.53:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#use-case-2-enterprise-mmis-shell-application]

### Use Case 2: Enterprise™ MMIS Shell Application

**Scenario Description:** The Platform Engineering team builds the shell that composes Claims, Provider, Member, Analytics, and Care Management remote modules for state MMIS portal users.

**Context:** Host/shell; not a Module Federation remote; requires SSR for initial context injection; centralized PingOne OIDC auth; multi-tenant state configuration.

**Guidance Application:** Next.js App Router. NextAuth.js + PingOne SDK per STD-TEC-NXT-003. `getServerSideProps` provides `MfeContextProvider` with `{ user, tenantId, permissions, config }` before first render. Remote modules consumed via dynamic import wrapped in React Suspense. CSP headers configured to allow CDN script sources; SRI hashes on `remoteEntry.js` loads.

**Success Factors:** Shell context delivered to modules before first paint; no client-side bootstrap delay visible in RUM (DynaTrace); PHI never in shell bundle or DevTools.

---
page_texts.54:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#use-case-3-member-self-service-portal-standalone]

### Use Case 3: Member Self-Service Portal (Standalone)

**Scenario Description:** The Care Management team builds a new member-facing portal for appointment scheduling, care plan review, and messaging — no Module Federation participation required.

**Context:** Standalone application; no federated remotes; lightweight interaction patterns; team has limited Webpack expertise.

**Guidance Application:** React + Vite. TanStack Query for API data. Zustand for UI state. PingOne SDK directly for OIDC auth (no NextAuth.js needed without Next.js). If Module Federation requirements emerge later, migration to Webpack 5 will be required — document this assumption in the ADR.

**Success Factors:** Build time <3 minutes; DX friction low for team; migration path to Module Federation documented in ADR.

[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#regulatory-compliance]

#### Regulatory Compliance

| Regulation | Requirements | Guidance Impact | Validation Approach |
|---|---|---|---|
| HIPAA Security Rule §164.312(a)(1) | PHI must not appear in module bundles, CDN assets, or serialized store state | PHI in any global state store (Redux DevTools, Zustand persist, localStorage) is a violation; PHI fetched at runtime only | Automated bundle scanning; PHI pattern regex in CI/CD; Redux/Zustand DevTools disabled in production builds |
| HIPAA Security Rule §164.312(b) | Audit logging of PHI access | User actions on PHI logged server-side; never in frontend bundles | Backend audit log coverage; verified by compliance team |
| Section 508 / WCAG 2.2 AA | Accessibility for federal government programs | All components (Next.js or React) must pass keyboard navigation, screen reader, and color contrast checks | Axe-core automated scan + manual audit per module |
| FedRAMP | CDN infrastructure must be FedRAMP-authorized | Module bundles hosted only on FedRAMP-authorized CDN (AWS CloudFront GovCloud or Azure Government CDN) | Infrastructure compliance review |
page_texts.58:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#organizational-compliance]

#### Organizational Compliance

- Technology selections deviating from this guidance require an **Architecture Decision Record (ADR)** and **Architecture Review Board** review
- All Next.js applications must comply with [STD-TEC-NXT-001](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/), [STD-TEC-NXT-002](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-002-error-handling-logging.md), [STD-TEC-NXT-003](../../../../standards/technology/nextjs/STD-TEC-NXT-003-frontend-design.md)
- All React (Webpack 5/MFE) remote modules and standalone React applications must comply with [STD-APP-FE-001](../../../../standards/application/frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md)
- Remote module bundle size must not exceed 500KB gzipped — enforced at CI/CD gate
page_texts.60:
[strategy/guidance/application/frontend-framework-selection/GUID-APP-TEC-001-nextjs-vs-react-selection-guidance.md#risk-assessment]

#### Risk Assessment

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technical | Next.js used as Module Federation remote breaks shell composition | Medium | High | Architecture Review Gate at project initiation; decision framework enforcement |
| Security / HIPAA | PHI in Redux/Zustand DevTools or persisted state | Medium | Critical | Zustand default (no DevTools); Redux DevTools disabled in production; PHI bundle scan in CI/CD |
| Operational | Shared dependency version mismatch causes duplicate React instance | High | High | Pin `requiredVersion` in all Module Federation configs; integration test suite verifies singleton |
| Strategic | Team introduces Vite outside the approved stack, fragmenting the toolchain | Low | Medium | STD-APP-FE-001 STD-FE-002 prohibits Vite for all new React applications; Architecture Review Gate enforces compliance |
